This generation of players is not accustomed to being spoken to or about in that manner. There is also the reality of how much loss the defense has suffered. Brian Burns, Tremaine Edmunds, and Chauncey Golston are gone for the season. Greg Newsome and Jevon Holland are out this week. item.title: Warriors coach Steve Kerr calls out Yaxel Lendeborg despite strong start to career
item.description: Kirby Lee-Imagn Images Warriors coach Steve Kerr calls out Yaxel Lendeborg despite strong start to career appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . Golden State Warriors coach Steve Kerr praised Yaxel Lendeborg’s offensive potential but criticized his defensive awareness. The rookie has impressed early, with Kerr previously praising his ability to lead Golden State’s offense. However, the coach believes Lendeborg still has significant room for improvement. “His weak-side awareness right now is very poor,” Kerr said in a video shared on X. The Warriors coach believes Lendeborg’s physical attributes should make him a more effective defensive presence near the basket. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) “With his size, he should be one of our best defenders at the rim,” Kerr added. Kerr also highlighted Lendeborg’s offensive versatility, describing the youngster as fearless and capable of dribbling, passing, and shooting. However, the coach pointed to a first-half possession when Lendeborg attacked a defender instead of choosing another option. “That’s gotta be a pull-up jumper. That’s gotta be a Euro step. That’s gotta be kick it out,” Kerr explained. The Warriors coach emphasized that decisions that worked in college might not translate against NBA defenders. Despite those concerns, Kerr remains confident that regular playing time and film sessions will accelerate Lendeborg’s development. “He’s playing a ton, and he’s gonna get all these reps,” Kerr said. The criticism comes after Kerr previously challenged Lendeborg to become more aggressive offensively. Golden State’s coaching staff now wants the rookie to improve his positioning and recognition when defending away from the ball. Kerr’s message is clear: Lendeborg has the talent to contribute immediately, but his defensive instincts must catch up. Kerr believes Lendeborg’s continued development will depend on how quickly he adjusts to the NBA’s defensive demands and learns from mistakes. item.description: Photo by Alex Grimm/Getty Images | Getty Images 46’ — Welcome back! The second half has begun. Halftime Observations Solid game from Bayern so far. The counterattacking scheme has somewhat worked, presumably another system the team is trying out for future use. That was an incredible goal by Dayot Upamecano. Won the ball outside his box, ran up and latched onto Michael Olise’s pass and finished a 1v1. Harry Kane probably taught him a thing or two. Lennart Karl is frustrating to watch at times, and today is one of those times. Konrad Laimer is obviously trying to get used to playing in midfield again after an extended period of playing as a right-back. 45+5’ — Half time! 45+3’ — Höler sees Jonas Urbig off his line and tries to shoot from his own half. item.description: (Photo by Todd Rosenberg/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Pittsburgh Steelers defeated the New Orleans Saints 16-10 in the NFL’s first game in Paris, France. It was a day in which points were hard to come by, but it felt as though the Steelers were in control from start to finish. As always, here is my weekly stock report after the Steelers moved to 5-2 on the season. Stock up RB Jaylen Warren Warren came into the contest already one of the most efficient running backs on a per touch basis in the NFL, and today was no exception. Warren carried the ball 18 times for 101 yards, good for 5.6 yards per carry. The back added three receptions for 36 yards to his line. After posting over 100 scrimmage yards in the first half, it was a quiet second half for offense in general. On a day where there weren’t many explosives on either side, Warren was once again the engine that kept the Steelers offense moving. Even with Dowdle increasingly involved, Warren is the clear leader in the Steelers running back split. ​TE Darnell Washington The Steelers’ best play in the red zone is when they throw the fade route to Darnell Washington. Freiermuth had a crucial drop in the fourth quarter that would have set the Steelers up deep inside Saints territory. It was a well-placed ball by Rodgers, but the tight end was unable to come down with it. As we just talked about, if the Steelers want to compete with the rest of the AFC, they will have to clean up small mistakes like this that force them into field goal situations rather than scoring touchdowns. ​Throwing fade routes to DK Metcalf This is not so much about DK Metcalf as it is about how much the Steelers tried to use this play today. Early in the red zone, the team called Metcalf’s number on a fade route, but the ball was simply uncatchable. Later in the first half, Rodgers tried to hit Metcalf on a similar play, but the ball was uncatchable again. The Steelers tried the play once again later in the game, and while the ball was catchable, it fell incomplete. Fade routes are a thigh-risk, high-reward kind of play that is fine in moderation, but it became the definition of insanity as they continued to call it. On a day in which points were hard to come by, it might have been smart to opt for higher percentage throws, especially in the red zone. item.title: Puka Nacua expected to play vs. Raiders
item.description: INGLEWOOD, CA - OCTOBER 12: Puka Nacua #12 of the Los Angeles Rams runs the ball during an NFL football game against the Buffalo Bills at SoFi Stadium on October 12, 2026 in Inglewood, California. (Photo by Cooper Neill/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Los Angeles Rams appear poised to have Puka Nacua available for their Week 7 matchup against the Las Vegas Raiders despite the star wide receiver suffering a minor calf injury during Thursday’s practice. While the injury raised some concerns heading into the weekend, Nacua is expected to suit up, giving Matthew Stafford and the Rams offense a significant boost as they look to get back on track. Nacua’s injury status headed into today is questionable. Rams are optimistic that WR Puka Nacua, who is questionable for Sunday’s game due to a calf injury, will play vs. the Raiders. Nacua was feeling better Saturday and, as one source said, “as long as there aren’t any setbacks, we feel good about him being available to play.” pic.twitter.com/mI22MZNcCj — Adam Schefter (@AdamSchefter) October 25, 2026 Nacua’s availability is especially important given the injuries he has already dealt with throughout the 2026 season. The third-year receiver has been a central figure in Los Angeles’ passing attack, and keeping him healthy will be critical as the Rams navigate the middle portion of their schedule. The latest calf issue is another reminder of the physical toll Nacua has endured this season. Although the injury is reportedly minor, any setback involving one of the team’s most important offensive players warrants attention, particularly with the Rams needing consistency from their passing game. Nacua previously battled a groin injury that forced him to miss Weeks 2 and 3. His absence during that stretch left Los Angeles without one of its most productive and dependable receiving options, putting additional pressure on Stafford and the rest of the receiving corps to compensate. That importance becomes even greater with Davante Adams placed on injured reserve and expected to miss 6-10 weeks with a ruptured hamstring. The Rams need their receiving group to remain productive, and having Nacua available would provide some much-needed stability as Los Angeles prepares to face Las Vegas. Still, the Rams will need to monitor Nacua’s condition closely. Even if he plays Sunday, managing his workload and ensuring the calf injury does not become a longer-term concern will be worth watching. For now, the expectation is that Nacua will be on the field against the Raiders.

item.title: Schefter: Seahawks among teams ‘expected to consider’ Jonathan Taylor trade
item.description: The Indianapolis Colts’ 2026 season has gone far from how they’d hoped, leaving them in a position to potentially sell off their stars for draft picks. One of those stars has repeatedly come up in fan conversations surrounding the Seattle Seahawks: running back Jonathan Taylor. However, it appears that it might not all be speculation, as ESPN’s Adam Schefter reported on Sunday that the Seahawks are one of four teams that have “pondered, or are expected to consider, the possibility of a trade for the star running back.” If they want the 27-year-old running back, the Seahawks would be competing with the Minnesota Vikings, Green Bay Packers and the Denver Broncos, according to Schefter’s report. Aside from the vague language there, a trade for Taylor makes sense on its face for the Seahawks. Taylor has been a premier back in the NFL since joining the Colts in 2020, is a three-time Pro Bowler and is coming off a season where he ran for 1,585 rushing yards and scored 18 touchdowns. With rookie Jadarian Price on IR and Zach Charbonnet out, there’s certainly hunger in Seattle to get their running game back on track. Seattle has spent most of their season rocking with Emmanuel Wilson and George Holani, who have struggled to generate a consistent, quality rushing offense. The issues with trading for Taylor emerge when looking at the value needed to acquire him and the contract extension that Taylor signed in the offseason. Taylor is owed $7 million in base salary in 2026, which balloons to $16 million in 2027 and then $18 million in 2028. For a franchise that, under general manager John Schneider, has not paid many running backs, that could be a tough sell. Notably, in Schefter’s report, the Seahawks are not explicitly tied to Colts All-Pro guard Quenton Nelson. All the NFL insider mentions in his article are that the 30-year-old offensive lineman could be on the market, with several “playoff-worthy” teams interested. The trade deadline sits on Nov. 10, so the Seahawks will have more time to ponder as they look to battle past a 3-3 start and continue their reign over the league.

item.title: Dayot Upamecano offers a comparison between Harry Kane and Kylian Mbappe
item.description: Bayern Munich and France international Dayot Upamecano has become the latest figure to weigh in on who should win this year’s Ballon d’Or, comparing his Les Bleus teammate Kylian Mbappé with his club teammate Harry Kane. As told to Gianluca DiMarzio (via @iMiaSanMia) , Upamecano shared his thoughts when asked which of the two should win the coveted award. Positioned uniquely as a teammate to both world-class forwards, Upamecano refused to pick a definitive favorite, choosing instead to highlight the distinct strengths each player brings to the pitch. “We all know that Harry can play as a defender, a midfielder and a striker – he can play in every position. For me, it’s an honor to be able to play alongside him. Kylian is a very explosive player who is incredibly fast and knows how to score goals. They are different kinds of players, but they both have the desire to score in every game, and that is their strength. I wish them both the very best, and we’ll see what happens,” said the defender. With the ceremony taking place in just two days, the winner will be revealed very soon. In the meantime, Upamecano’s analysis likely reflects what the voters are thinking, too. Of the two, some may argue that Kane has had the stronger season in terms of performance, especially considering England’s run at the FIFA World Cup, but Mbappé remains one of the premier strikers in top-flight football. Do you agree with Upamecano’s assessment of the two? Who should win the award on Monday? Let us know in the comments!

item.title: Glass-half-full time: Why are you still optimistic about the Commanders?
item.description: The Commanders are 1-4-1. That’s where we’re at after some tough one-score losses, quarterback injuries and, simply put, unacceptable game mismanagement. All, however, is not lost. A one-win team is still somehow in the divisional race considering how bad the other three teams are. Like, check the standings . The Giants have three wins in six chances entering Week 7, and that’s the target to shoot for. And the Giants have a quarterback controversy. The Eagles have lost Jalen Hurts and most of a previously excellent offensive line. And the Cowboys are struggling, a standard for the Jones era. So, despite the fact that it at times feels like Washington’s sky is falling, the Commanders can still pull out a division title. True freaking story. I’m in the former camp. I truly believe the Commanders can turn the corner. Here are a few reasons why. You’ll be able to follow the rationale, guaranteed. Here are some bullet points on why the Commanders can win the division. These aren’t detailed observations. They’re simply reasons to be optimistic starting with a Week 8 meeting with the Philadelphia Eagles coming off the bye. Jayden Daniels turns into JD5: The young quarterback can legit carry a team when he’s on one. The third-year pro is trying to find a balance between being a playmaker and an operator of David Blough’s system. There’s a fair belief that he’ll get there. If he can get on 2024’s level, Daniels can bring the Commanders to great heights. Odafe Oweh wakes up: The Commanders biggest free-agent purchase can get scorching hot collecting sacks — he did so last year — and this would be a great time to go on a run. The Commanders pass rush is essential to defensive success. That has been proven in the early going, with coverage unable to hold up for long. Play callers lessen their learning curves: The Commanders have a pair of rookie (NFL) play callers in offensive coordinator David Blough and defensive coordinator Daronte Jones, and we’ve seen some mistakes in game planning and game-day game planning. Washington must be more consistent and help play to their players’ strengths moving forward. Here’s believing they can do that. Penalties get cleaned up: The Commanders have been plagued by penalties, especially the pre-snap variety that have wiped out some explosive/game-changing plays in games that went the other way. Fewer flags, especially all those false starts and illegal shifts. That should be something easy to fix. That’s why I think there’s optimism for better Commanders football after the bye. item.title: Michael Carrick says waving to fans after Bournemouth thrashing ‘wasn’t a farewell’
item.description: Michael Carrick insisted he was not saying farewell to Manchester United after their 3-0 defeat to Bournemouth but admitted he does not know if he will be sacked. United have made their worst start to a season for 40 years and lost their last two games by three goals, following Wednesday’s 4-1 thrashing by Como , and Carrick was taunted by Bournemouth supporters with chants of “sacked in the morning”. He was still serenaded by United fans as he went down the tunnel but claimed: “It wasn't a farewell from me.” He said he had only had a short conversation after the game with the United hierarchy and is not sure if chief executive Omar Berrada and sporting director Jason Wilcox will dismiss him. “Just briefly like always after a game, but nothing out of the ordinary,” he added. “I will see what happens. I totally understand the situation. “I'm not expecting anything in particular, to be honest. I am carrying on as normal. I love this place. I'll always do what I feel is going to be the best for the football club, whatever decision is made on anything really. So that's kind of it. You know, I'm not expecting anything either way.” Carrick insisted the United players are hurting as their nosedive continues but admitted he has not spoken to them all. “There's a lot of emotion in the changing room right now, there's a lot of disappointment, there's a lot of the boys quite hurt, disappointed,” he said. “It's not like they don't care, or they want to be in this position. The ones I've spoken to - I've not spoke to everyone individually, the ones I have spoken to, it's affecting them a lot.” Carrick said he was left with a variety of feelings as he thanked the United fans for their backing. “Mixed emotions for the supporters to respond in that way,” he said. “To feel the connection and appreciation from the supporters, I feel it and appreciate it a lot.”

item.title: Texas QB Arch Manning Goes Viral for What He Said After Ole Miss Win
item.description: AUSTIN, TEXAS - OCTOBER 24: Arch Manning #16 of the Texas Longhorns warms up before the game against the Ole Miss Rebels at Darrell K Royal-Texas Memorial Stadium on October 24, 2026 in Austin, Texas. (Photo by Tim Warner/Getty Images) Getty The No. 19 Texas Longhorns secured what many deemed a must-win game Saturday night against the No. 7 Ole Miss Rebels at home in Austin. Texas led 24-3 at halftime but somehow squandered that lead, allowing Ole Miss to tie the game at 24 in the second half. However, the Longhorns found their rhythm in the fourth quarter and won 34-27. Quarterback Arch Manning completed 18 of 30 passes for 212 yards, one touchdown and two interceptions. He also scored two rushing touchdowns, including the go-ahead score when the game was tied at 24. Manning Has Viral Message for Holly Rowe After Win Several weeks ago, Manning went viral for the wrong reasons when he commented during a media interview about a funny AI video depicting his head coach, Steve Sarkisian, punching ESPN reporter Holly Rowe. Although Manning didn’t intend any harm with his comment, he faced considerable backlash and apologized shortly afterward in a statement on social media. He also reached out to Rowe personally. On Saturday night, Rowe interviewed Manning on the sideline after the game. Before the interview ended, Manning told her she needed to cover more Texas games because the Longhorns are now 3-0 when she’s on the sidelines. “I think you need to start doing our games more this year. We’re 3-0 with your this year,” Manning said. Rowe responded, “Hey, we’ll take it.” Well done all around by Texas QB Arch Manning. https://t.co/bHXBOHBUyJ — Adam Schefter (@AdamSchefter) October 25, 2026 The interview was shared across several platforms, but ESPN’s Adam Schefter posted it on Sunday morning. In less than two hours, the clip surpassed 500,000 views on X. College Football Fans React on Social Media “Alright that made me really like Arch Manning,” a fan said. Someone else added, “That really meant a lot to her.” Another person wrote, “That boy’s mama taught him right.” “That’s actually really sweet,” a fan shared. Another posted, “Arch has no idea how much that meant to her!” One more person commented, “This is cool. You can tell people dragging both of them blew things way out of proportion. They absolutely had a conversation, he said this on purpose (in a good way) and it meant a lot to her (also a good thing). Cool moment for sure.” This article was originally published on HEAVY The post Texas QB Arch Manning Goes Viral for What He Said After Ole Miss Win appeared first on HEAVY .

Getty The Cleveland Browns could look to add to their defense ahead of the Nov. 10 NFL Trade Deadline. Cleveland is atop the AFC North and has been a major surprise this season. The Browns could use help on offense, or Cleveland could go all-in on defense to further bolster their pass rush. The Browns will go on the road to play the Tennessee Titans in Week 7. Cleveland Browns Urged to Acquire Will McDonald IV Getty Browns urged to acquire Will McDonald IV to bolster their pass rush. The Browns have been linked to several defensive stars ahead of the deadline, and they could look at acquiring a former first-round pick. NFL analyst Daniel Popper of The Athletic named the Browns as one of the best fits for New York Jets pass rusher Will McDonald IV. “McDonald survived the Jets’ fire sale ahead of last year’s trade deadline. In the spring, the Jets exercised his fifth-year option for $13.75 million fully guaranteed in 2027. He is on a cheap base salary for 2026 in the fourth year of his rookie deal,” Popper wrote . “The Jets have depth at edge rusher, and rookie David Bailey is emerging, though free-agent addition Joseph Ossai is now dealing with an ankle injury. Ossai also missed the first two games of the year. McDonald is a twitchy rusher with some diversity in his attack, including an inside spin move. Best fits: 49ers, Patriots , Browns, Cowboys.” McDonald will be in line for a hefty contract extension, but he’s already under contract through 2027, so Cleveland could use it as a year-and-a-half rental. The Jets took McDonald 15th overall in the 2023 NFL Draft, and he’s had some moderate success in the NFL. His best season came in 2024 when he appeared in all 17 games, recording 28 tackles, 10.5 sacks, and 11 tackles for a loss. This year, he’s recorded 12 tackles and 2 sacks, along with a forced fumble and a fumble recovery . Cleveland Makes Decision on Another Potential Trade The Browns are expected to be buyers ahead of the trade deadline. But they have also been linked to dealing away receiver Jerry Jeudy. However, NFL insiders Adam Schefter and Ian Rapoport made it clear Cleveland isn’t likely to trade Jeudy. “The Cleveland Browns find themselves atop the AFC North with a surprising 4-2 record and plenty of promise. They reached that following a stirring win last week that included a clutch 33-yard catch-and-run from Jeudy, whose name has been the subject of plenty of trade speculation. … (But) sources say his chances of being traded is viewed as less likely,” the article read . “The Browns aren’t shopping Jeudy at all, and the price is high. It would take a premium deal to get Cleveland to move on — even if general manager Andrew Berry is open to discussing any deal. But as of right now, a Jeudy deal seems unlikely.” So, it’s likely the Browns will be adding players instead of subtracting ahead of the deadline. This article

item.title: Liverpool boss Iraola on beating Brighton and Wirtz injury worry
item.description: Liverpool boss Iraola on beating Brighton and Wirtz injury worry Andoni Iraola has played down fears over Florian Wirtz after the Liverpool midfielder was forced off with an ankle problem during the 2-0 win over Brighton. Wirtz will now be assessed by the club’s medical team, but Iraola said the early signs suggest the injury is not serious. “Unfortunately, he had to leave the pitch with a small twist of the ankle,” Iraola said. “It doesn’t look very big but we are playing every three days so we need to see where he is.” The victory extended Liverpool’s winning run to four games, with Iraola particularly pleased by the way his side started. “Very happy for today, very happy overall for these four wins,” he said. “I think we had today a very good opposition in front, similar to Villarreal the other day – teams that technically are really good. “It’s difficult to defend them a lot of times. I think today the key was how we started. “We needed a stronger start, be aggressive, recover the ball, win our duels, be dangerous in transitions. “I think we’ve done it and it has been a different game from the last ones, where we’ve conceded first and after you need a comeback. “Today, I think we’ve started better and the game has gone differently.” Iraola also praised Alexander Isak and believes the striker will continue to score if Liverpool can provide him with the right service. “He’s a striker, if we can put him in those positions, we can provide him with crosses, good situations, he will score the goals,” he said. “I think it’s a matter of, in this case, Bradley [Barcola] winning the duel, going one-v-one, being faster than the opposition and finding good spots.”

item.title: Guardians Set To Lose 2 First Basemen in Free Agency
item.description: KANSAS CITY, MISSOURI - SEPTEMBER 26: Jo Adell #7 and Nathaniel Lowe #46 of the Cleveland Guardians celebrate clinching the American League Central Division title after defeating the Kansas City Royals at Kauffman Stadium on September 26, 2026 in Kansas City, Missouri. (Photo by Jay Biggerstaff/Getty Images) Getty The Cleveland Guardians spent the entire 2026 MLB season trying to figure out the first base position. It’ll be another point to focus on in the offseason with both Nathaniel Lowe and Rhys Hoskins due to be free agents. The Guardians certainly wish they were still playing right now rather than thinking about first base, but that’s not how things went for them. They made it six games in the ALCS but were eliminated by the Tampa Bay Rays. Now, the Rays are down 2-0 in the World Series to the NL champion Milwaukee Brewers, and the Guardians are at home. The lockout will complicate things further, but their first base outcome actually seems relatively straightforward. Guardians Could Lose 2 Lowe and Hoskins are two veteran free agents, and both seem likely to end up elsewhere. They aren’t the types of players that the Guardians generally re-sign. The Athletic’s Zack Meisel has also made clear that it’s logical for Cleveland to move on because of the younger players they have at the position. “Lowe and Hoskins seem unlikely to return, given the club has Kyle Manzardo and top prospect Ralphy Velazquez to handle first base,” Meisel writes . Manzardo struggled this season and was sent down after the Lowe trade, but it seems likely that he’ll get another chance in the 2027 season. Velazquez is the exciting one. He’s got a great baseball name, Ralphy, and he can really rake — he possesses immense power to all fields. If Lowe and Hoskins do both leave, it’ll just be a couple of guys departing that didn’t quite work out in Cleveland. Nathaniel Lowe Trade Could Be Costly The Guardians traded two players for Lowe when they got him from the Cincinnati Reds : Juan Brito and Alejandro Rivera. Rivera is a teenage pitching prospect who has a long way to go but could develop into a useful player. Brito is the more immediate aspect of the deal. The second baseman always hit well in the minor leagues but hadn’t done so in Cleveland, and he didn’t have a job once Travis Bazzana arrived in the majors. But after getting traded to Cincy, Brito quickly stood out with his bat for the Reds. He hit better down the stretch than Lowe did. If Brito turns into a quality MLB hitter, it’ll hurt that the Guardians traded him for just a few so-so months from Lowe. Lowe was a positive presence on Cleveland’s roster, but the lack of hitting down the stretch and in the playoffs definitely hurt the Guardians’ chances of reaching their biggest goals this season. item.description: Amber Flora, the professional wrestler who is known as Amber Nova in the ring, was arrested early on Friday in Orlando, facing DUI and refusal to undergo DUI testing charges, based on public records. Flora, 34, was released later that morning after posting $1,000 bail on each charge, totaling $2,000. According to jail records TMZ initially obtained, Flora was arrested at 5:40 a.m. and released at 10:07 a.m. Flora attended a mandatory court hearing on Saturday, with court docket records indicating a compliance date of November 2. item.description: Matthews’ family ‘very excited’ as London Palladium hosts event 70 years after first award at Blackpool town hall When football’s dignitaries assemble on Monday at the London Palladium for the Ballon d’Or ceremony it will be a far cry from the first awards 70 years ago. That was held in the slightly less glamorous surroundings of Blackpool town hall, where Stanley Matthews was presented with the prize by Gabriel Hanot, the visionary editor of L’Équipe who came up with the idea of crowning the world’s best player every year. A specially commissioned china plate was also handed over by the town’s mayor before the 41-year-old Matthews, who was famously teetotal, gave a short speech. “He might have had a double carrot juice that day,” says his son, Stanley Matthews Jr, who will attend this year’s awards with his sister, Jean, and her two daughters. “There was no ceremony. ‘Here’s your Ballon d’Or, well done’, sort of thing. But obviously it’s grown over the years, and now it’s a huge event. We’re very excited.” Continue reading...

Chelsea were meant to have grown. Xabi Alonso had even praised his side’s emotional control and ability to manage awkward spells during the buildup, but perhaps that was asking for trouble. item.title: Change captain? Play the kids? How to solve the problems at Manchester United
item.description: The beleaguered Michael Carrick’s job is on the line, but there are steps he can take to revive the stricken club The big question as Bournemouth arrive for Sunday’s 2pm kick-off at Old Trafford is whether Michael Carrick will show his authority by stripping the captaincy from Bruno Fernandes and/or dropping Manchester United’s five-times player of the year. On Friday, Carrick refused to deny he may do so, but the bigger picture concerns whether cashing in on the Portuguese and his fellow mutineer, Lisandro Martínez, in the winter window would be prescient to initiate a new era. Fernandes and Martínez are out of contract in the close season (the club has an extra year’s option in both cases) and, judging by recent behaviour, intend to leave. So yielding, say, £40m and £25m respectively for them in January would allow investment as the rebuild begins. Even a few days on, Fernandes’s words in Como seem incredible: “It’s a decision from the staff to not press man-to-man and sometimes leave space behind and try to get the ball, wait for them, but sometimes when you give space to these teams they get confidence,” he said after Wednesday’s 4-1 humiliation. Fernandes’s open questioning of the tactics is a challenge to the head coach’s authority and we wait to see how/if Carrick will face it down. If Carrick acts and proves he is not a lame duck then even if he is removed a favour is done for his successor. Continue reading...

item.title: Football Daily | Mourinho is ready for his clásico return – stock up on popcorn, folks!
item.description: Sign up now! Sign up now! Sign up now? Sign up now! Football Daily has never had much time for conspiracy theories. Lee Harvey Oswald dunnit, Stanley Kubrick didn’t fake the moon landing, Vinícius Jr doesn’t have a body double and Miranda isn’t a secret traitor. But our Spidey senses picked up when the UK government announced their Be Ready campaign on Thursday night. In case you missed it, or live outside the UK and couldn’t care less about this weird little island, we’ve lifted this from our news story : “Every Briton is being urged to stock up to nine litres of bottled water and three days’ worth of food in new government guidance designed to ensure that households can survive a weather, cyber or other serious emergency. The Be Ready campaign is aimed at persuading people to stock up with supplies to last 72 hours, amid growing official concern about the impact of the climate crisis, technological dependency and hostile state threats.” Would it not be much easier all round if the two big clubs in Manchester simply swapped all playing and coaching staff before the next round of fixtures? United would finally get the squad that Bruno Fernandes and Lisandro Martínez clearly feel they deserve, one of serial winners who are worthy of the club’s fine history (and free of the whiners). Meanwhile, City would might get a team that would make them (somewhat) competitive in the lower tiers where they’re surely headed. And a manager who has coached there quite recently. Sure there’d be a few grumbles from the fans, but more importantly in the current football climate, think of all the potential new shirt sales, and the Us-Against-the-World mentality that Enzo Maresca would be able to instil in his team whose own supporters would even hate them. And no-one would even have to move house. It’s a win-win solution. Although, no, it’s United; so probably a win-high-scoring-draw-against-Wycombe solution” – Justin Kavanagh. Like all right-minded people, I only read Big Website to get my fill of news and information (ahem …). However, I did come across a recent piece in The New Yorker on James Daunt, the chief suit of the US book chain Barnes & Noble (no relation). The billionaire Russian oligarch, Alexander Mamut, asked him 20 years ago how much it would cost to buy Waterstones, and when he was told it would be £40m, he looked pleased and just said, ‘That’s less than Fernando Torres’, before adding, ‘It’s not even half a boat’. Odd reference points these billionaires” – Noble Francis. May I be the first of 1,057 Daniels to say thank you for the good luck message at the end of Thursday’s Football Daily. It has put a little extra pep in my step today” – Daniel Mee. This is an extract from our daily football email … Football Daily. item.title: Is el clásico still the world’s biggest match? Three questions before Barcelona v Real Madrid
item.description: The fixture’s relevance waned as the Messi-Ronaldo rivalry faded. Can Lamine Yamal and Mbappé lift it into a new era? For the best part of a decade, el clásico was more than just soccer’s biggest fixture. It was the defining narrative. At the peak of the Lionel Messi v Cristiano Ronaldo era, there were clásicos everywhere. Yes, when the two historic rivals clashed on the pitch, but also in the voting for the Ballon d’Or every year and in so much of the discourse around the sport. As the Messi-Ronaldo rivalry faded, though, so too did the clásico ’s relevance. This isn’t to say matches between Barcelona and Real Madrid no longer matter. They always have and always will. In 2026, however, it’s difficult to measure a clásico ’s standing. Is it still the sport’s biggest fixture? Continue reading...

item.title: Chaotic state of football in Brazil epitomises a nation where greed has conquered glory | Jonathan Liew
item.description: The national game merely reflects the mood in a divided nation which is going to the polls with very little faith in the power of democracy Look, cards on the table: I don’t know for certain, and nor do you, whether Flávio Bolsonaro – the man widely tipped to become the next president of Brazil after Sunday night’s election – really did steal an island from Richarlison. There are lawyers involved, claims and counter-claims, and in any case, adjudicating land ownership disputes between right-wing strongmen and Tottenham reserve-team strikers lies very much beyond this column’s spectrum of expertise. It’s why, for example, this newspaper took no official position on the well-publicised battle between Rodrigo Duterte and Vincent Janssen over that Polynesian isthmus. According to Richarlison, a few years ago he purchased an island off the southern coast of Rio de Janeiro, and has the documentation to prove it. Richarlison says Bolsonaro tried to buy it from him, and when he refused a lawyer named Willer Tomaz simply turned up and annexed it. “These guys took the island without spending a penny, as far as I know,” Richarlison claimed in an Instagram video that has been viewed more than 31 million times. Tomaz has accused Richarlison of lying, arguing that he has a public deed registered at the notary’s office. Bolsonaro, for his part, has denied any connection with the island in question and described Richarlison’s intervention as “politically motivated”. Continue reading...

item.description: Max Dowman may get a chance, Spurs need to find balance at Stamford Bridge and Axel Disasi must make amends Premier League top scorers After seven games, Nottingham Forest’s record is eerily similar to last season: five points, five goals scored. A year ago Forest’s eighth game was a 3-0 home loss to Chelsea that marked the end for Ange Postecoglou , the second of four managers to occupy the dugout last term. There is no suggestion that Oliver Glasner is under similar scrutiny yet, but the Austrian needs to find solutions for the league’s lowest scorers. Morgan Gibbs-White is available after missing the narrow defeat by Arsenal , while Liam Delap may benefit from a return to familiar surroundings – 12 of his 14 career Premier League goals were scored for Ipswich, six of them at Portman Road. “What we need to improve is getting [Delap] into more positions where he can score,” Glasner said before Friday evening’s game. “He’s one of our best finishers.” Gary O’Neil also lacks a standout scorer, but he is squeezing goals out of his side. Eight different Ipswich players have scored in seven games; only Brighton and Brentford can better that total this season. item.title: Manchester City have been a joy to watch but they became detached from their roots | Philipp Lahm
item.description: City behaved much like other top clubs but their rule-breaking deserves to be punished. The Bundesliga, where members have a controlling stake, can show the way forward Do we have to reassess Manchester City now? In my columns, I have repeatedly engaged with this club and its key figures. Looking back at what I have written over the years, I believe it remains beyond question that the team have achieved greatness. I always loved watching them: they were a true unit on the pitch, a finely tuned orchestra. I would also write all over again that the conductor, Pep Guardiola, masters his craft like few others. I could recognise his teams even if they were wearing the wrong shirts and the game was broadcast in black and white – by the passes, the distances between the players and the intelligence of their interplay. It is no wonder Guardiola inspires others to become managers; look at Vincent Kompany, Mikel Arteta, Enzo Maresca, and perhaps some time Ilkay Gündogan and Rodri. Continue reading...

item.title: Brighton are the apex B club – their next target should be a Champions League place | Jonathan Wilson
item.description: Diego Gómez’s wondergoal in a five-star demolition is just the latest in an impressive run of results for the south coast team Sign up for our free newsletter here For two or three years now, it’s been standard to nod approvingly at how well-run Brighton, Brentford and Bournemouth are, and to move on. What else is there to say? It’s true, of course – these are sides who have made the most of relatively limited resources. But there’s also an underlying assumption in the designation: that these are clubs who have no higher aspiration, that their limit is earning praise for upper mid-table finishes. This season, perhaps, offers an opportunity to change that. Other than Arsenal, every major club is undergoing significant transition. Manchester City may have started the season with seven straight wins, but there’s every chance the punishment for their multiple breaches of Premier League regulations takes them out of the race for the top five. item.title: Europe is a blast – but more a curse than a blessing if you are not a Premier League super-club I Jonathan Wilson
item.description: The four Premier League clubs playing in the lesser continental competitions face each other on Sunday – but three are struggling domestically The sun shone. The temperature was in the high 20s. There was a mood of great conviviality. If you were struggling with the official allocation, it turned out you could just email the president of Torreense and he’d sort you out. Were these “Nuno-tickets” real? It turned out they were. Not only that, but you could sit anywhere you wanted in a stadium too big for the game and, if you happened to have gravitated to the comfortable hospitality seating at the back of the lower tier, the beer was inexplicably free. Locals in Leiria seemed bewildered but could hardly have been more accommodating. A beer pump had been installed outside a patisserie on the Praça Francisco Rodrigues Lobo, whose owner soon found fans happy to help stack empty barrels if that facilitated the free flow of Sagres. “There was a meeting at the town hall to explain these are not hooligans,” said the owner of a radical leftist flammkuchen restaurant between the square and the cathedral. “They told us the club comes from the labour movement and I found that very interesting.” And how had she found the fans? “Noisy, but with a quirky sense of humour.” Continue reading...

item.title: James McClean: ‘Wearing the poppy was just never going to happen’
item.description: The former Republic of Ireland international on growing up in a community still reeling from the Troubles and the controversy that scarred his career “The perception of me is that, basically, I am a madman,” James McClean says calmly. “I’m outspoken. I’m a loudmouth. I’m very opinionated and I hate all things British. That’s from people who don’t know me. The reality is quite the opposite. I’m pretty boring. I go training, go home and switch off. A lot of my days are quite bland, quite basic.” McClean sounds as sane as he looks gaunt on a bleak Monday in Derry. He spent 14 years in English football and the fact that he is now at war with his own club, Derry City, can’t obscure the fact that he is the fifth-most-capped Republic of Ireland international, having played 103 times. “People define success in different ways,” he says, “but I’m the only footballer from the north of Ireland to win over 100 caps for Ireland. I played 150 Premier League games over five seasons, 800 professional games and won a lot of individual accolades. I count that as success and don’t look back with regrets.” Continue reading...

item.description: The Frenchman, who has been named the best male footballer in the world by the Guardian, has benefitted from PSG’s focus on the team rather than individuals What makes a good player great, and a great player the best? This question has been occupying me since 2014, when the Guardian first asked me to contribute to its inaugural Next Generation feature . My job was to look for a France-based talent born in 1997 who could go on to have a stellar career. After a great deal of research, I narrowed it down from my shortlist of five by asking questions not about the players’ football ability, but about other attributes: resilience, adaptability, decision-making, creativity, work ethic, response to feedback and willingness to learn. Qualities we cannot see, and are harder to measure. Continue reading...

item.title: Aitana Bonmatí makes Guardian top 100 history with third title in a row
item.description: The margin may have got smaller but the brilliant Spanish midfielder makes it a hat-trick of No 1 finishes They say the best things come in threes, and Aitana Bonmatí has written herself into the Guardian’s top 100 history as the first player to finish at the top of the tree for a third consecutive year. Last year the majestic midfielder emulated her Barcelona and Spain teammate Alexia Putellas by winning for a second year running , but the 27-year-old has now gone one better, establishing herself once again at the top of the women’s game.
